artists.biography:
Matthew Charles "Matt" Berry (born 2 May 1974) is an English actor, writer, comedian and musician. Berry is perhaps best known for his appearances in The IT Crowd, Garth Marenghi's Darkplace, The Mighty Boosh, and Snuff Box. He is renowned for his deep voice; he has voiced several advertisements, most notably for Volvic, The Natural Confectionery Company, Absolute Radio, and MoneySupermarket.

As a musician, Berry composed all the music for Snuff Box, as well as the music for AD/BC: A Rock Opera, which he co-wrote with Richard Ayoade. AD/BC was a half-hour parody of overblown musicals in general and Jesus Christ Superstar in particular, telling the story of the innkeeper who allowed Mary, Joseph, and the baby Jesus to sleep in his manger. AD/BC was broadcast in December 2004 and featured Fulcher and Mighty Boosh stars Julian Barratt and Noel Fielding. He also performed a song for an episode of Garth Marenghi's Darkplace entitled "One Track Lover", a spoof of cheesy romantic 80s songs.

perplexity.description:
Music for Insomniacs (2014) by Matt Berry is an ambient electronic album that serves as a tribute to 1970s synthesizer pioneers. Released on the Acid Jazz label, the album consists of two extended instrumental tracks that blend ethereal Moog and Mellotron textures with subtle found sounds and layered synths, creating a meditative and immersive soundscape. The music evokes a dreamy, floating atmosphere reminiscent of Brian Eno’s ambient works and classic library music, designed specifically as a soothing experience for those suffering from insomnia.

Positioned in Berry’s discography after Kill the Wolf (2013), Music for Insomniacs marks a distinctive experimental detour from his folk and rock-oriented albums. It highlights his versatility as a multi-instrumentalist and composer, focusing entirely on instrumental, synth-driven compositions without vocals. The album’s structure features a dynamic progression, opening with a nod to Mike Oldfield’s Tubular Bells and evolving through lush, cinematic passages that blend ambient calm with moments of synth-pop energy.

Critically, the album was appreciated for its ambitious scope and textural richness, though it remained a niche release within Berry’s broader output. Commercially, it reached number 96 on the UK Official Charts, reflecting modest mainstream impact but solidifying its status as a cult favorite among fans of ambient and electronic music. Overall, Music for Insomniacs stands as a unique and introspective entry in Matt Berry’s catalog, showcasing his deep appreciation for vintage synth sounds and ambient composition.
